assessment: While decades of research findings have supported the idea that action attenuates predicted touch, a recent finding has countered this, proposing that action actually enhances predicted touch and that the previously observed attenuation is due to tactile contact. The present study rigorously probes these alternative hypotheses with three pre-registered experiments. They show that previous enhancement findings are due to the lack of a proper baseline condition of externally generated sensation with which to compare. In light of the recent opposing findings, the current paper is important and presents compelling evidence in favor of the sensory attenuation theory.
